statement:
fix(mysql)!: keep the native IF instead of changing it to CASE [CLAUDE] (#8409)

* fix(mysql)!: keep the native IF instead of expanding it to CASE [CLAUDE]

IF is a native MySQL function, but sqlglot expanded every exp.If into a
CASE expression, so even MySQL's own IF(a, 1, 2) did not round-trip.

IF takes exactly three arguments, so a missing false branch is emitted as
NULL, matching what the BigQuery and Snowflake generators already do. A
CASE that was written as one is untouched.

Verified on StarRocks 3.5.18 that both forms agree, including a NULL
condition and the two-argument form rendered as IF(cond, value, NULL).

fix(mysql): SHOW CREATE TABLE generating a syntax error [CLAUDE] (#8408)

* fix(mysql): qualify the name in SHOW CREATE instead of emitting FROM [CLAUDE]

SHOW CREATE TABLE db.tbl was generated as SHOW CREATE TABLE tbl FROM db.
SHOW CREATE takes a possibly qualified name and has no FROM clause, so
the result is a syntax error on both MySQL and StarRocks.

The FROM suffix is still used by the SHOW statements that do take it,
such as SHOW COLUMNS and SHOW INDEX.

fix(parser)!: raise on a duplicate OFFSET instead of overwriting it [CLAUDE] (#8367)

LIMIT x, y splits into a limit and an offset, and the offset half went into
its slot without the duplicate check the clause above it uses, so an OFFSET
that was already parsed got silently overwritten. It now raises the way a
duplicate LIMIT does, and ErrorLevel.IGNORE still degrades to the old
overwrite.
